description:

Doctor bead (plan §12.2, frankensonos §12.2 analog): zestroku doctor — what is broken and how to fix it.

Check registry in zestroku-core; each check: id, prerequisites, returns pass/warn/fail/skip with detail + evidence + concrete remedy. Prereq-failed checks skip, not fail.

Checks: data dir + store; SSDP responder per device; targets.toml seeds; each device :8060 device-info fetch + latency; tier posture (probe map re-run, §4 map as structured data); store migrations current; suspend-vs-absent discrimination.

Read-only: never mutates device state. Output: table with remedies or --json; exit 0/6/7 pass/warn/fail. Also MCP doctor and GET /doctor.

- [ ] check registry trait + at least the seven checks above implemented and unit-tested with fixture transports
- [ ] planted negative: a check that mutates state fails review (doctor asserts read-only)
- [ ] exit codes 0/6/7 verified; --json shape documented

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] check registry trait + at least the seven checks above implemented and unit-tested with fixture transports
- [ ] planted negative: a check that mutates state fails review (doctor asserts read-only)
- [ ] exit codes 0/6/7 verified; --json shape documented

## AMENDMENT 2026-10-10 (director, reality-check R1)
Add check `lan-policy` (prereq: at least one seeded or discovered device). It classifies a failed direct connect: errno 65 / EHOSTUNREACH from zestroku while a platform tool answers (`/usr/bin/nc -z -G2 <host> 8060` exits 0) => FAIL with code LAN_BLOCKED_BY_OS_POLICY and remedy "run through the resident daemon (agents) or `ssh -o BatchMode=yes localhost <cmd>`; the macOS Local Network permission of the launching process tree is the suspected gate (inferred, unproven)"; the platform tool also fails => FAIL with code DEVICE_UNREACHABLE (network or device down, not policy).
WHY: a roughly three-hour misdiagnosis on 2026-10-10 (an upstream-library-bug theory, a std-fallback transport, a drafted upstream issue) came from the missing platform-tool control.
ACCEPTANCE:
- [ ] `lan-policy` unit-tested with an injected connect error (65) and an injected platform-tool result: policy vs unreachable classified correctly.
- [ ] planted negative: removing the platform-tool control makes both cases classify as policy and the test goes red; ECONNREFUSED is classified as neither.
NO-CLAIM: names the symptom class, not the OS mechanism.

title: M8: policy.toml — rate limits, allowlists, quiet hours, one choke point
description:
Policy bead (plan §12.5, frankensonos §12.5 adapted — mutation-focused, no media knobs): policy.toml + the choke point.

policy.toml in the data dir: max keypresses/second + launches/minute per client; per-client tool allowlists (keys: client id cli|mcp-stdio|loopback-http); quiet hours during which mutations require explicit confirmation even for cli. Over-limit -> POLICY_DENIED, logged.

Identity: surface + principal (cli / mcp-stdio / loopback-http). Unresolved identity never fails a request; it gets read-only tools. Choke point: every mutating call on every surface goes through one authorize -> snapshot -> execute -> log path in zestroku-core.

title: Tier discovery: probe, record, and use the observed access tier (replace the ZESTROKU_TIER env stand-in)
description:
WHAT: (a) pure `classify_tier` in zestroku-core: query/apps 200 => Permissive; 403 whose body is exactly "ECP command not allowed in Limited mode." => Limited; any other outcome (different 403 body, 5xx, unreachable, malformed) => Unknown; the result and a probe_map (command class -> open/403/404/untested) are recorded in the access_tier table and devices.access_tier with probe_at; (b) `zestroku info <host>` prints `tier=<limited|permissive|unknown>` and whether tv-active-channel is present; (c) `key` and `launch` read the latest recorded tier (re-probing when unknown or stale); Unknown refuses (exit 3, message says to run `zestroku info`); ZESTROKU_TIER remains only as an explicit override and the audit row records `tier_source=env-override`; (d) `zestroku devices` persists each reconciled device to the store.
WHY: crates/zestroku-cli/src/mutate.rs says the tier "comes from discovery (m7c)" but today it is an unchecked env var; the first live launch (m7e leg, 2026-10-10) needed ZESTROKU_TIER=permissive. grep shows no non-test writer for the devices, apps, capabilities or access_tier tables, so the m7d store is unwired for inventory. Plan section 1 says `info` shows the access tier.
ACCEPTANCE:
- [ ] [a] unit tests for Permissive, Limited, Unknown; planted negatives: a 403 with a different body => Unknown (never Limited); a 200 with garbage XML => Unknown.
- [ ] [b] `info` output test against a loopback fixture server (zestroku-sim once proven).
- [ ] [c] an Unknown-tier mutation exits 3 and the server-side request log shows zero POSTs; planted negative: removing the `tier_source` recording turns an audit-row test red.
- [ ] [d] after `devices --no-ssdp --targets <seeds>` the store holds one row per found device and keeps them across reopen; live (via ssh, witness agent): both devices report tier=permissive and two rows are stored.
NO-CLAIM: the tier is observed, not authenticated; this is not a defense against a hostile device.

title: Resident zestroku daemon: launchd + loopback/tailnet bind guard + peer attribution
description:
WHAT: (a) a launchd LaunchAgent that runs `zestroku serve` resident, started from a tree that owns macOS Local Network permission, so agents never open LAN sockets themselves; (b) listeners bind loopback plus the tailnet address only, never LAN or wildcard (refuse at startup otherwise); (c) peer attribution for each connection via tailscale whois, carried into the action log principal; (d) Tailscale Funnel refused by construction. Pattern source: frankensonos fsonos-tailscale (cite, do not copy).
WHY: agent panes get instant EHOSTUNREACH to LAN IPs on this Mac (measured 2026-10-10: same binary fails from the pane tree, works via ssh localhost); a resident daemon turns a per-run permission problem into a one-time deployment step. Josh approved the architecture 2026-10-10 (verbatim: "yes i approe all of this").
ACCEPTANCE: [a] plist installs and `launchctl print` shows the job running; a client in an agent pane gets device-info for both live devices through the daemon over loopback (live, via a second witness); [b] startup with a LAN or wildcard bind address exits non-zero before listening (in-tree #[test]); [c] an unattributed peer is refused or logged as unknown, never defaulted to an owner principal (test with a fake whois); [d] enabling Funnel in config fails startup (test); [a-d] each has a planted negative that goes red when the guard is deleted.
CONTEXT: depends on m7c (serve). Needs the owner to approve the LaunchAgent install on this Mac.

## AMENDMENT 2026-10-10 (director, reality-check R1)
Added scope: [e] once the daemon path is proven, remove the ZESTROKU_TRANSPORT=std fallback and the test-only `--transport-probe` subcommand from the shipped CLI (both were added in 39bed22 on the since-refuted upstream-defect theory); [f] in normal operation the daemon is the only zestroku process that opens LAN sockets.
ACCEPTANCE (added):
- [ ] [e] a grep-based in-tree test asserts neither `ZESTROKU_TRANSPORT` nor `--transport-probe` remains; planted negative: re-adding either turns it red.
- [ ] [f] with the daemon up, `lsof -i` of a client run shows no LAN-address sockets from the client process (control: the daemon process shows them).
NOTE: plan section 7 says "no resident daemons" for doctors and gates; this is the product daemon the owner approved on 2026-10-10 ("yes i approe all of this"); the coordinator amends the section 7 wording at countersign.
